A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same House of Dextra study, and their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. Although v5 Figure 7 extends below the page boundary, its correlation plot is preserved in Appendix Figure 18, so the evidence remains comparable.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulation experiments, real-world hand evaluations, controller comparisons, and morphology sensitivity analyses, including Tables 1–3 and Appendix 9.

after.justification: v5 retains original simulation and real-world results, including baseline comparisons, object-rotation measurements, and the appendix controller and morphology analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 substantially revise the specified architecture. v3 describes finger-link nodes, joint edges, and GNN-embedding-conditioned control; v5 specifies a six-node palm/finger-slot graph for design scoring and a separate one-hot morphology input to PPO. This changes the reported representation and policy conditioning, although the PDFs do not establish whether the underlying implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate in-hand rotation, tabletop grasping, and flipping, retain the LEAP morphology study, and test blind real-world rotation on the same documented object collection. The new introductory reference to 18 objects does not establish additional coverage: Sections 5.1 and 9.3 still report 17, and the object illustrations are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains RoboGrammar, Monte Carlo, the MPPI variant, vision-based single-cube LEAP, blind LEAP, and the no-fine-tuning variant. The individual-PPO and MPPI/CEM comparisons in Appendix 9.1 also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Section 4 replaces 128 randomized environments per design with 2048 parallel environments per evaluation cycle. This is a revised protocol statement, but the different aggregation units prevent inferring a per-design increase or rerun. v5 also introduces an inconsistent 18-object count in the introduction while retaining 17 in the experimental sections.

E4.justification: The MPPI/CEM failure study, cross-embodied versus individual PPO comparison, hardware-parameter sensitivity analyses, and real-world morphology cases are retained. v5 Figure 8 captions an existing MPPI/CEM image sequence rather than adding a new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: The reward-curve shading and appendix correlation, sample-count, and curve-fit annotations are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional seed information, repeated-run protocols, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results are retained, including Table 1's 3.3 and 1.85 rad/s values and Table 3's rotation times. A limited quantitative statement is removed: v3 Figure 5 reports grasps under 0.1 seconds, whereas the corresponding v5 Figure 6 says only 'quick grasps.' Section 5.2 retains the under-half-second result.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces the link/joint graph and root-width/depth definitions with a fixed star graph and revises the morphology-conditioned state definition. These are substantive mathematical-definition changes. The bi-level optimization formulation and PPO objective retain their basic structure, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain morphology-conditioned co-design, manufacturable modular hand generation, efficient evaluation, deployment within 24 hours, and task-specific morphology advantages. The revised wording and more explicit introductory object count do not establish a different central scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v5 removes the explicit limitation that design diversity and convergence were not systematically analyzed, including the associated risks of mode collapse and insufficient exploration. No corresponding analysis is added. The remaining task-specificity, modular-component, and neglected-material-property limitations are retained.

D1.justification: New Algorithm 1 documents search initialization, group-specific evaluation, candidate-dependent Gumbel temperatures, duplicate handling, probabilistic ancestor replay, and minibatch updates beyond the earlier prose. Section 3.2 also explicitly identifies the family checkpoint used for blind-policy fine-tuning. Hardware specifications and domain-randomization tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and Section 7 retains the same positioning relative to co-design, cross-embodiment learning, and sim-to-real research.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on the notation and method explanations, with smaller wording corrections, updated publication headers, and an added acknowledgment. The section order and most experimental, related-work, and appendix prose remain intact. The introduction inadvertently repeats the contribution summary and concluding overview.

P2.justification: The combined task montage and reward plot become redesigned Figures 5–6, adding hand-to-curve callouts and rotation views. The exploded hardware illustration is redrawn, the existing MPPI sequence gains a numbered caption, several figures and tables move, and Algorithm 1 adds a new display. The resulting layout clips Figure 7 below page 9, hiding its lower portion and caption.

improvement.justification: The revised representation description and Algorithm 1 improve technical specificity, but the PDFs do not resolve whether the changed architecture and evaluation statements describe corrections or different experiments underlying the retained results. v5 also introduces duplicated introductory prose, an 18-versus-17 object inconsistency, and a clipped figure, while removing the diversity/convergence limitation without new analysis. These documentation gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
